title: pdfsys.doc/1
description: L2 publish format. Two Parquet tables joined on image_id: `documents` (one row per PDF, carrying the reading-order block list) and `images` (one row per unique image blob). The interleaved and image-text-pair views are projections over `documents.blocks`, not separate storage. Canonical implementation: pdfsys_core.dataset + pdfsys_cli.dataset_writer.

BlockType.title: BlockType
BlockType.description: Block-level classification. The four furniture types (page_header, page_footer, page_number, aside) are page decoration and are excluded from the rendered `text` by default.

BBox.title: BBox
BBox.description: Normalized bounding box, [0, 1], top-left origin, y down. Null when the source coordinates could not be normalized — an absent bbox is honest, an unnormalized one silently corrupts every downstream crop.

Block.title: Block
Block.description: One block-level unit in document reading order. Position in the array IS the interleaving — there is no separate image/text alignment structure.

idx.description: Zero-based reading-order index within the document. Dense; equals the array position.

page.description: Zero-based page this block was extracted from.

text.description: Content. Encoding follows the Segment contract: text/title/list = Markdown, table = HTML, formula = LaTeX, code = source text. Null for image/chart, whose pixels live in `image_id`.

level.description: Heading level for `title` blocks; null otherwise.

caption.description: Human-authored caption attached to an image / chart / table. Multiple caption lines are newline-joined.

footnote.description: Footnote attached to an image / chart / table.

alt.description: Model-generated description of the image (MinerU VLM output). Kept separate from `caption` so a consumer can choose ground truth over synthetic text.

image_id.description: SHA-256 of the image bytes; join key into the images table. Non-null for image/chart blocks and for table blocks whose crop was kept.

mentions.description: Indices of blocks in the same document whose text references this figure/table by label ("as shown in Fig. 3"). Empty when unknown or unlinked.

Document.title: Document
Document.description: One row of the documents table — one published PDF.

id.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source PDF bytes. Same identity as ExtractedDoc.sha256.

provenance.description: Opaque upstream JSON (license, crawl batch, policy tier). Not parsed by pdfsys.

text.description: Markdown rendering of `blocks`: furniture dropped, images as `![](img://<image_id>)` with the caption following as its own paragraph. Redundant with `blocks` by design — see the spec for the measured cost. Null when the shard was written with include_text=false.

page_ends.description: Character offset in `text` at which each page ends; length equals n_pages. Recovers page granularity without a second copy of the text (same encoding as FinePDFs).

blocks.description: The authoritative record. Ordered by reading order.

image_ids.description: Distinct image ids referenced by this document, in first-use order. Denormalized so a join can be planned without reading the nested column.

n_chars.description: Length of the rendered text. Populated even when `text` is null.

images.description: Only present when the shard was written with embed_images=true, which inlines the blobs instead of using the images table.

ImageBytes.title: ImageBytes
ImageBytes.description: HuggingFace `datasets.Image` wire struct. Decodes via cast_column("image", Image()) with no conversion.

path.description: `<image_id>.<format>`; informational only — images are addressed by content.

Image.title: Image
Image.description: One row of the images table — one unique image blob per shard. Content addressing dedupes the letterheads and stamps that repeat across a scanned corpus.

width.description: 0 when the header could not be parsed.

Pair.title: Pair
Pair.description: One row of the optional materialized image-text pair view. Derived from documents.blocks; never a source of truth.

source.description: Which tier supplied the text, best first: content (caption + own transcription, e.g. a table crop with its HTML), caption (human ground truth), alt (model-generated), mention (body text referencing the figure by label), context (adjacent text blocks).
